name: Mahalalel
overview: Mahalalel is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Perez according to Nehemiah 11:4. The biblical record provides limited details about him beyond this lineage connection within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Mahalalel means 'praise of G-d [El],' reflecting a proper name with a theistic meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear expression of worship and reverence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mahalalel as the father of Shephatiah, an inferred relationship, and as a descendant of Perez, an explicit relationship found in Nehemiah 11:4. Beyond these connections, no further family details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mahalalel's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily genealogical, linking him to Perez and thus situating him within the tribe of Judah. His mention in Nehemiah highlights his place in the post-exilic community, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people through established family lines. Though not a prominent character in narrative events, his role as a link in the lineage of Judah emphasizes God's providential preservation of His chosen people.
